text: Economics is a social science that studies the laws of resource allocation, production, distribution, exchange and consumption, aiming to explain the economic behaviors and social phenomena of individuals, enterprises and countries through theoretical models and empirical analysis. This major aims to cultivate talents with a solid foundation in economic theory, quantitative analysis ability and practical application ability, who can engage in economic analysis, policy formulation, management decision-making and other work in government departments, financial institutions, enterprises and scientific research units. Students need to systematically master the core theories of microeconomics and macroeconomics, learn to use mathematical and statistical tools to analyze economic issues, and understand the logic of real economic operations (such as market mechanisms, international trade, and financial markets).
